deviceKey.name: Authorization

text.example: A vote to end debate so the Senate can move to a final vote. On a bill it needs three-fifths of senators sworn in, 60 when the Senate is full. Passing cloture doesn't pass the bill.

source.description: The rule or law the line rests on

VoteExplainer.description: What this kind of vote is, in a line; null for a question Floor has no line for (never a guess)

MeasureSponsor.description: A bill's sponsor; null for a nomination and for a bill whose sponsor is not in the members table

title.description: A bill's short title where it has one, else its full title; a nomination's nominee, or the post for a military nomination that names nobody

summaryLead.description: The opening of the bill's CRS summary (the text the bill route serves as `summary`) without its title line: the first sentence, or two when the first is short, cut at a sentence end, at most about 320 characters. stage.description: A bill's stage on the road to law, as BillListItem.stage, so a list can draw its progress without a request per bill; null for a nomination and for a bill the worker has not staged

position.description: A nomination's position title; null for a bill
position.example: United States Circuit Judge for the Tenth Circuit

forBillId.description: For a House special rule ("Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 2102) ..."), the id of the bill it brings to the floor: the first one its title names when it names several. Null for anything else

MeasureSummary.description: null for a procedural vote that refers to no measure

partyTotals.description: Per-party counts, as on `VoteDetail`; empty for an election, which has no yea or nay

Position.description: candidate is only used on Speaker elections

choice.description: Candidate named in a Speaker election

partyTotals.description: Per-party counts. An election reports its party split in candidateTotals instead.

candidateTotals.description: Which candidate each party voted for. Only populated when kind = election.

positions.description: How the members named in ?members= voted. Empty when the query names none.

allOf.description: What was voted on, or null for a procedural vote that refers to no measure

votes.description: Yea/nay votes counted: those where the member voted yea or nay and their party was not itself tied

contactForm.description: The office's own web form. Null for most House members, whose offices list none: use the House's "Write Your Representative" form (https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative) instead

address.example: 2436 Rayburn House Office Building Washington DC 20515-3312

heading.description: The site's own section heading, as written

quote.description: Verbatim from the archived page: checked by machine to be on it, up to spacing and quote marks

headline.example: bring critical supply chains and manufacturing back home

topic.description: One of the 32 policy areas (GET /v1/topics), or null

electionYear.description: The race that won this term

snapshotUrl.description: The Wayback Machine capture the promises were read from

pageUrl.description: The issues page within the site; null when the home page was read

promises.description: In the page's order; empty unless status is promises

text.description: As posted; a YouTube video's title

mediaUrl.description: A thumbnail: YouTube's, or the first Bluesky image

MemberPost.description: No like or repost counts: Floor stores none

PostLinks.description: Profiles on networks Floor cannot read for free: links only

text.description: As posted; a YouTube video's title

mediaUrl.description: A thumbnail: YouTube's, or the first Bluesky image

WallPost.description: A MemberPost with whose it is

posts.description: Every asked-for member's posts together, newest first

unreadable.description: Asked-for members with no YouTube, Bluesky or Mastodon account: they post only where Floor links out (X, Facebook)

office.description: Shown apart, never in the bar

title.description: Written by the AI, in neutral wording

url.description: The Google News link to the article

allOf.description: null when the release does not break the rest out

polls.description: Polls naming the member, fielded within the last 90 days, newest first

placeGeoid.description: Census place GEOID, for a city

news.description: Last 7 days, newest first, at most 20; tone null (not AI-read)

kind.description: From FEC's committee type for another candidate's own committee ('Candidate committee'), else its organization type or leadership-PAC designation; null when FEC classifies the committee as nothing

cycle.description: The election this campaign is for

receipts.description: Total raised this campaign to date, as the campaign reported it

other.description: Transfers, the candidate's own money, refunds and other receipts

committees.description: Biggest PAC givers by direct amount. Party and joint fundraising committees are excluded — neither is a PAC check (lesson 23)

MemberFunding.description: funding is null for a member FEC has no current-campaign totals for

owner.description: Whose asset it is, as filed; dependent means a dependent child

amount.description: The amount range exactly as filed. Never a number

notifiedAt.description: House only: when the filer learned of the trade

filedAt.description: When the report listing it was filed

daysToFile.description: Days from the trade to the filing

pastDeadline.description: Filed more than 45 days after the trade, the STOCK Act's outer limit. A fact about the dates, not a finding

status.description: paper: a scanned filing Floor holds only as a link (it reads none by machine, and has not transcribed this one); unparsed: an electronic filing Floor could not read

reason.description: Why there is no data, when enabled is false

year.description: The calendar year the report covers

transcribed.description: true when Floor's AI transcribed these rows from a paper (handwritten or scanned) filing: label them AI, say they may contain errors, and link the original

annual.description: The latest annual report Floor has read; null when there is none

trades.description: Trades in the last 12 months, newest first

paperFilings.description: Filings in the same window Floor holds only as a link: the annual report and trade reports a client must not present as empty

Disclosures.description: No totals and no estimates: every value is a range as filed

stateLower.description: State house/assembly district, as Open States names it; null where there is none (Nebraska)

place.description: The Census Incorporated Place, or null outside one

elect.description: Members-elect for these seats (the state's Senate seats, this House seat)

pending.description: These seats whose race is not called

choice.description: Candidate named in a Speaker election

allOf.description: null for a procedural vote that refers to no measure, e.g. a motion to adjourn

summary.description: Latest Congressional Research Service summary, plain text

url.description: The page to share; opens in the app where it is installed

text.description: The share sheet's line, to send with url. Neutral: what happened or is next, never a side

quote.example: extends several expiring programs and authorities

section.description: The bill section, as CRS labels the paragraph; null when it names none

ai.description: Always true: this line was written by AI

allOf.description: null when no purpose line survived verification

categoryText.example: Items that may be considered under suspension of the rules

billId.description: null for a resolution not yet numbered, or a bill not in Floor's catalog yet

label.description: The citation; as the source prints it when the bill is unknown

title.description: The bill's plain label (BillListItem.label) when known, else the source's own text

sourceText.description: What the source printed for the item, e.g. a suspension's title with ", as amended"

removedAt.description: Set once the item was taken off the week's list; it is kept so it can be shown as pulled

proForma.description: A pro forma session: the Senate meets for seconds and does no business

program.description: The Daily Digest's "Program for" text, verbatim but for whitespace. Null until the Congressional Record for the day before is out, usually the next morning

recordIssue.description: The Congressional Record volume/issue the program is from

inSession.description: true when the House has published a schedule for the week; null when it has not (not yet, or a week it is out). The House publishes none for a district work period, but an unpublished week is not reported as one

sourceUpdatedAt.description: When a source last edited anything shown for this week

allOf.description: Only this chamber's votes; null for both

when.description: Only when this holds; null for always

questions.description: The roll call questions it explains, matched ignoring case and spacing

part.description: 0 unless the Senate split the nomination into parts

citation.description: As the Senate cites it on the roll call

nomineeName.description: null for military nominations, which promote officers in bulk; show the position instead

positionTitle.example: United States District Judge for the Southern District of Ohio

description.description: Congress.gov's full sentence, including the "vice ..." clause

inSession.description: Sitting now, or within 15 minutes of convening

convenesAt.description: Next (or current) convening, when the chamber has published it

checkedAt.description: When the live worker last polled this chamber

openedAt.description: The floor's own time for the vote (House only)

announcedAt.description: When the worker first saw a floor source name it

postedAt.description: When the worker first saw the roll call XML, polling live; null if it was backfilled

allOf.description: What is being voted on. An open vote is not linked to its bill yet, so this is read from the roll call's bill reference (`billRef`) when the bill is in the catalog; null for a procedural vote or an unknown bill

chambers.description: Empty until the live worker has run

votes.description: Open votes named in the last 24 hours, then votes that went final within `since`; newest first

lastNewDataAt.description: When a successful run last stored anything. A scheduled job keeps lastSuccessAt fresh even when upstream stops publishing or nothing is found, so a long gap here, not `stale`, is what shows that

lastError.description: The error of the latest run with an outcome, if it failed; null once a later run succeeds. A run that never recorded an outcome within an hour reads as "abandoned run"

bills.description: Bills in this topic in the Congress

label.description: A plain short label: the short title, or a deterministic rewrite of a long CRS title. The full title is `title`.
label.example: Improving Care in Rural America Reauthorization Act of 2025

allOf.description: Where the measure stands on the road to law; null until the worker has staged it. adopted = a resolution agreed to by every chamber it needs (it never goes to the President); failed = a chamber voted it down (Congress.gov's own marker); vetoed = vetoed and not overridden.

stalled.description: Not settled (law, adopted, vetoed, failed) and no action in 90 days

hasFloorVote.description: At least one recorded roll call on it

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last

billNumber.description: The query read as a bill number ("hr 1013"), so `bills` holds exact matches only

floorScheduled.description: "Scheduled for the floor": on a chamber's weekly floor schedule. Default on

chamberVote.description: "Passes or fails a chamber, with the score". Default on

lawOrVeto.description: "Becomes law or is vetoed". Default on

committee.description: "Committee action": hearings, markups, reported. Default off

throughTopics.description: "Through topics too": bills in a followed topic alert as if followed. Default off

id.description: A Bioguide ID, a Floor bill id (`119-hr-1013`), or a topic's canonical name (`Health`, as /v1/topics names it)

howVoted.description: Alert when the vote is final: how a member voted, or that a followed bill was voted on. Off items are still listed, because "A vote opened" covers votes involving any of them. Ignored for a topic

apnsToken.description: The alert token; null without notification permission

voteOpened.description: "A vote opened": a push alert when a vote involving these opens

allOf.description: The "Bills you follow" switches. Omitted means the defaults

get.summary: Members, bills and topics in one search
get.description: A bill number in any spelling ("hr 1013", "H.R.1013", "s.j.res.197") returns that bill and nothing else. Otherwise words match bill short titles, titles and CRS summaries (Postgres full-text), topic names, and sitting members exactly as `/v1/members?q=` reads them (the same reader, up to 60, Senate first): a name with accents, hyphens and apostrophes folded ("velazquez", "ocasio cortez"), a state by name or code ("Texas", "N.Y."), or a seat ("TX-35", "DC-1"). `chamber` narrows the members only. Companion bills (the House and Senate versions of one measure) are separate results and are not linked to each other.

allOf.description: Only this chamber; omit for both

put.summary: Register this phone for alerts and Live Activities, or replace its registration
put.description: The whole registration each time: tokens, "A vote opened", every member and bill with its "How they voted" switch, every followed topic, and the "Bills you follow" switches (`billAlerts`). Identified by the `Authorization: Device <key>` header (a random 32-byte key, base64url); no account, no address. Rate limited, 30 a minute per caller, shared with the other device routes.
